staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout. The metadata vulnerable commit differs, but this local snapshot is the exact source whose line numbers match `patch.diff`, `sanitizer_trace.txt`, and the saved ASan stack.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42533504 (aom): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target av1_dec_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42533504
bug_description.original_source: sample metadata / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer's heap-buffer-overflow against the staged checkout `cae8fbe572bec3443b89d9be858ff0abb7020f1b`. In the exact 194-byte witness, `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` sets `tile_mode=1`, `ext_tile_debug=1`, `is_annexb=0`, and `threads=31`, so `av1_decode_tg_tiles_and_wrapup()` takes the large-scale row-mt path. `read_ext_tile_info()` then materializes `tile_col_size_bytes = 1` and `tile_size_bytes = 1` from attacker-controlled frame bits. Inside `get_ls_tile_buffers()`, the first non-last column length byte at `frame + 23` is `0x3c`, so after `data += 1` the vulnerable assignment publishes `tile_col_data_end[0] = frame + 84` even though the real tile-group end for this OBU is `frame + 47`. The same unchecked size advances `data` to `frame + 84`, reinterprets out-of-group byte `0x0f` as the second column length, and publishes `tile_col_data_end[1] = frame + 100`. Last-column parsing then restarts from `frame + 100`; the four one-byte tile headers there are `0x01`, `0x01`, `0x28`, and `0x02`, whose top bits are clear, so `get_ls_tile_buffer()` takes the direct publication arm and stores `tile_buffers[3][2] = { data = frame + 149, size = 3 }`, i.e. file offset 193 with length 3. A row-mt worker passes that exact slice together with the real tile-group boundary `thread_data->data_end = frame + 47` into `setup_bool_decoder()`. Because `read_is_valid()` is `len != 0 && len <= (size_t)(end - start)`, `start > end` underflows the subtraction, accepts the invalid slice, and lets `aom_reader_init()`/`od_ec_dec_init()` seed `od_ec_dec_refill()` with `buffer = file + 193` and `end = file + 196`; the second byte fetch is the saved 1-byte out-of-bounds read at file offset 194. The staged patch fixes the bug by checking both that the column-length field fits in the remaining payload and that the decoded `tile_col_size` does not move `tile_col_data_end[c]` past `data_end`.

source.description: Source. In the large-scale ext-tile header for the crashing witness, attacker-controlled bits materialize the widths of the later tile-column and per-tile size fields.
source.value_from: In the exact PoC, IVF control byte `0xb7` makes `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` set `tile_mode=1` and `ext_tile_debug=1`, and the saved stack later reaches `decode_tiles_row_mt()`. In that large-scale path, this `read_ext_tile_info()` parse yields `tile_col_size_bytes = 1` and `tile_size_bytes = 1` before `get_ls_tile_buffers()` consumes the tile-group payload.

sink.description: ASan sink. Entropy-decoder initialization dereferences the invalid worker slice published for the exact last-column tile and performs the observed out-of-bounds read.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `aom_dsp/entdec.c:94:26` on address `0x611000000382`, exactly 0 bytes past the 194-byte region `[0x6110000002c0,0x611000000382)` allocated by libFuzzer. Static reconstruction of the exact witness shows this is the second byte read from the published slice `{ data = file + 193, size = 3 }`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After decoding a non-last tile-column length, the vulnerable code turns it into a column end pointer without first checking that `tile_col_size` fits in the remaining bytes `data_end - data`.
root_cause.note: For the exact witness, this unchecked assignment turns `frame[23] = 0x3c` into `tile_col_data_end[0] = frame + 84` even though the real tile-group end is `frame + 47`. The staged patch inserts both the missing pre-read guard for `tile_col_size_bytes` and the post-read guard `tile_col_size > (size_t)(data_end - data)` immediately before this assignment.

tainted_value_origin.description: Concrete tainted column length. At the start of the exact tile-group payload, this statement reads the first non-last tile-column length byte later trusted to derive `tile_col_data_end[0]`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Step 1 fixes `tile_col_size_bytes = 1`, so this call consumes exactly byte `frame[23] = 0x3c` (file offset 67) and materializes `tile_col_size = 60`.

parser_admitted.description: The exact witness sets `tile_mode=1`, `ext_tile_debug=1`, `is_annexb=0`, and `threads=31`, so `av1_decode_tg_tiles_and_wrapup()` takes the large-scale row-mt decoder path. This `read_one_tile_group_obu()` call admits the OBU_FRAME tile-group payload whose bytes later reach `get_ls_tile_buffers()` as `data = frame + 23` and `data_end = frame + 47`.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 relies entirely on static reconstruction of the saved witness and staged source; it did not add any new runtime measurement beyond Stage 01's saved crash artifacts.

The staged vulnerable checkout at `gt_results/arvo_42533504/_work/src/aom` is on commit `cae8fbe572bec3443b89d9be858ff0abb7020f1b`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. All line anchors below are resolved against the staged checkout because that is the exact source snapshot used for Stage 01 reproduction.

The PoC contract is intentionally witness-specific. The saved artifacts prove only the exact 194-byte file and its reconstructed offsets and header bytes; they do not justify a broader claim about neighboring AV1 layouts or all oversized tile-column lengths.

coarse_trace.summary: The large-scale ext-tile header reads the one-byte width fields later used for non-last column lengths and per-tile headers.
The first non-last column length `0x3c` is trusted without bounds checking, so `tile_col_data_end[0]` is published beyond the real tile-group payload and the parser state jumps out of that payload.

An out-of-group byte is reinterpreted as the second column length, `tile_col_data_end[1]` becomes `frame + 100`, and last-column parsing restarts from that corrupted pointer while the true last-column end stays at `frame + 47`.
The exact last-column headers `0x01, 0x01, 0x28, 0x02` all take the direct arm, and the helper publishes `tile_buffers[3][2] = { data = file + 193, size = 3 }`.
A row-mt worker passes that exact tile slice together with the real tile-group boundary into `setup_bool_decoder()`, where `read_is_valid()` accepts it through unsigned underflow.
Reader initialization seeds `od_ec_dec_init()` on the invalid 3-byte slice, setting the entropy-decoder end pointer past the 194-byte witness.
`od_ec_dec_refill()` reads byte 193 and then byte 194, producing the saved 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. In the crashing large-scale ext-tile frame, attacker-controlled header bits materialize `tile_col_size_bytes = 1` and `tile_size_bytes = 1` for later column-length and tile-header parsing.
At tile-group entry `data = frame + 23` (file offset 67), this reads the first non-last column length byte `0x3c`, so `tile_col_size = 60` for column 0.
`data` advances to `frame + 24`, the first byte after the length field and the exact base pointer later used by the root-cause arithmetic.

Root cause. Without checking `tile_col_size <= (size_t)(data_end - data)`, the code publishes `tile_col_data_end[0] = frame + 84` even though the real tile-group end for this OBU is only `frame + 47`.
The same unchecked `tile_col_size` advances the initial column-size pass to `frame + 84`, outside the real tile-group payload.
At the out-of-group pointer from step 5, this reinterprets byte `frame[84] = 0x0f` as the second non-last column length, so `tile_col_size = 15` for column 1.
`data` advances to `frame + 85`, the base pointer used for the second out-of-range column-end calculation.
Using the out-of-group length from step 6, the same unchecked assignment publishes `tile_col_data_end[1] = frame + 100` for column 1.
For the last column `c = 2`, the helper keeps the true extent: `tile_col_data_end[2] = data_end = frame + 47` (file offset 91, exclusive).

When the second pass reaches last-column `c = 2`, parsing restarts from the corrupted pointer `tile_col_data_end[1]`, so `data = frame + 100` while the last-column limit from step 9 remains `frame + 47`.

From the corrupted last-column start in step 10, the earlier row iterations read headers `0x01`, `0x01`, and `0x28`. Their top bits are clear, so the copy predicate is false each time; under the underflowed checks against step 9's real `data_end`, the helper direct-publishes rows 0-2 of column 2 and advances `*data` to `frame + 148`.

At `*data = frame + 148`, the row-3 header byte is `0x02`. Its top bit is clear, so the copy-mode condition is false and the direct arm yields `size = 3` with the tile payload starting at `frame + 149`.

With `size = 3`, `*data = frame + 149`, and the real last-column `data_end = frame + 47`, the subtraction `data_end - *data` underflows when cast to `size_t`. The guard therefore does not reject the 3-byte slice.

Because step 12 stayed on the direct arm and step 13 did not reject it, row 3 column 2 is published as `tile_buffers[3][2] = { data = frame + 149, size = 3 }`. This maps to file offset 193 with the post-publication parser pointer advanced to file offset 196.
Each row-mt worker receives the real tile-group boundary from `decode_tiles_row_mt()`. For the exact OBU payload, this `data_end` is the same `frame + 47` limit captured in step 9.

The crashing worker passes the exact published slice from step 14 together with the real boundary from step 15 into `setup_bool_decoder()`. Among all published cells, only `tile_buffers[3][2]` has `data = file + 193` and `size = 3`, so it is the unique `tile_buffer` consistent with the saved ASan crash.

For the worker slice from step 16, `start = file + 193`, `len = 3`, and `end = file + 91`. Because `start > end`, the pointer subtraction underflows when cast to `size_t`, so this predicate incorrectly returns true.
Because step 17 accepts the slice, reader initialization sets `buffer = file + 193`, `buffer_end = file + 196`, and `dec->end = file + 196` before immediately calling `od_ec_dec_refill()`.
Sink. `od_ec_dec_refill()` first reads file byte 193 and then advances to read file byte 194, which matches AddressSanitizer's report of a 1-byte read exactly past the 194-byte allocation.

sanitizer_ground_truth.crash_summary: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in od_ec_dec_refill at /src/aom/aom_dsp/entdec.c:94:26, with stack od_ec_dec_refill -> od_ec_dec_init -> aom_reader_init -> setup_bool_decoder -> tile_worker_hook_init -> row_mt_worker_hook.

cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Static reconstruction of the exact witness shows that `get_ls_tile_buffer()` direct-publishes `tile_buffers[3][2] = { data = frame + 149, size = 3 }`, `tile_worker_hook_init()` passes that slice together with `thread_data->data_end = frame + 47` into `setup_bool_decoder()`, `read_is_valid()` accepts it through unsigned underflow, and `aom_reader_init()` seeds `od_ec_dec_refill()` on the resulting `[file + 193, file + 196)` range.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run `docker exec gt-arvo_42533504-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'` fed `poc` to `/out/av1_dec_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `od_ec_dec_refill` with stack `od_ec_dec_refill -> od_ec_dec_init -> aom_reader_init -> setup_bool_decoder -> tile_worker_hook_init -> row_mt_worker_hook`.

format.name: exact staged AV1 witness
format.contract: Grounded only for the exact 194-byte file `gt_results/arvo_42533504/poc` with sha256 `a42d6fc3a708e418fd47bfceff0551861bd60bc5e4e9e66280216671903fe37b`. In this witness, IVF control byte `0xb7` makes the fuzzer set `tile_mode=1`, `ext_tile_debug=1`, `is_annexb=0`, and byte `0x9e` makes `threads=31`. The admitted OBU_FRAME tile-group payload reaches `get_ls_tile_buffers()` as `data = frame + 23` and `data_end = frame + 47`; the vulnerable first non-last column length `0x3c` moves `tile_col_data_end[0]` to `frame + 84`, an out-of-group byte `0x0f` becomes the second column length, and last-column parsing restarts from `frame + 100`. The last-column headers `0x01`, `0x01`, `0x28`, and `0x02` all take the direct arm, so the exact crashing publication is `tile_buffers[3][2] = { data = file + 193, size = 3 }`. The row-mt worker then passes that slice together with the real tile-group end `file + 91` into `setup_bool_decoder()`, `read_is_valid()` underflows, and `od_ec_dec_refill()` performs the saved read at file offset 194. No broader AV1 input class is claimed.
